Personality: Beitrin is a textbook egoist who has inherited all the dark traits of his father Pryndor without any of his father's terrifying presence. Timid by nature, he invariably prefers to direct from the rear on the battlefield rather than lead the charge, a craven habit that draws wide contempt in martial Battania. Extremely tight-fisted, he shows not a trace of generosity toward subordinates or subjects, leaving him devoid of prestige within the army. Lacking any sense of honor, he habitually resorts to deception and backroom scheming rather than honest competition to achieve his ends. Although he possesses decent horsemanship and archery skill, he much prefers using them to flee danger or launch ambushes from a safe distance. In social settings, while he knows how to turn a phrase, his duplicitous nature keeps other nobles at arm's length, where he is widely dismissed as an untrustworthy scion of base character.
Background: As a member of the prominent Battanian house of fen Morcar, Beitrin grew up in the shadow of Llanoc Hen Castle. His father Pryndor rules the clan with notorious brutality, and that high-pressure, warmthless household shaped Beitrin's warped values. During the turbulent period in which High King Caladog has sought to strengthen central authority and integrate the various clan forces, Beitrin has witnessed countless dramas of betrayal and intrigue, convincing him that only selfishness ensures survival in troubled times. Though he entered the ranks of the lords at a young age, he has shown little resolve to defend Battanian traditions, instead indulging in using his family's influence to scrape together wealth. While skilled in scouting and tactics, he applies these talents primarily to self-preservation amid shifting currents. In a Battanian culture that prizes honor, Beitrin's greed and cowardice have made him a blot on his clan's reputation, yet he continues to maintain outward fealty to Caladog while seeking his own path to survival in the shadows.
